To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the supplementation of polyphenols from grape seed and grape skin, grape marc meal and spent hops as feed supplements does not affect the expression of genes and proteins involved in the hepatic inflammatory, antioxidative and cyto-protective system, phase I and II metabolism, the endoplasmatic reticulum stress response and the hepatic status of the antioxidative system of healthy piglets.

supplementation of GSE or SH, as sources of polyphenois, to piglets does not alter hepatic pathways linked with inflammation, the antioxidant, cytoprotactive, xenobiotic and unfolded protein response systems in healthy pigs.
supplementation of GSE or SH as sources for polyphenols does neither affect hepatic inflammation, antioxidative status, cytoprotection nor stress of the endoplastic reticulum in healthy pigs.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the question whether dietary supplementation of polyphenol-rich plant products exerts anti-inflammatory and cyto-protective effects in the liver and whether these effects are mediated by changes in the expression of inflammatory genes, genes of the antioxidative and detoxifying system, genes of the endoplamsic reticulum (ER) stress and the xenobiotics system.

the influence of dietary polyphenols on the expression of hepatic genes involved in inflammation, the antioxidant system, the cytoprotective response and stress of the endoplasma reticulum in piglets.
the question of whether the polyphenolic compounds of GME and SH have a cytoprotective effect in the liver of healthy piglets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
supplementation of polyphenols from GME or SH does not influence the liver of healthy piglets, but it might have beneficial effects in the small intestinal mucosa of piglets.

the polyphenol-rich plant products from grape seed, grape marc meal or spent hops used in the present study have no anti-inflammatory, cytoprotecting or antioxidant effects in the liver and plasma of healthy piglets.
supplementation of GSE or GME as sources of polyphenoic compounds does not exert anti-inflammatory and cyto-protective effects in the liver in healthy piglets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effects of polyphenols in the liver of healthy animals are not pronounced.
supplementation of GSE or SH as feed additives does not have any effects on the liver in healthy pigs.
the polyphenol-rich plant products used in the present study are not suitable to improve the hepatic antioxidant status and the cytoprotective mechanisms in piglets.
The main takeaway from our work is that
polyphenols from GME or SH have no anti-inflammatory or cytoprotective effect on the liver of healthy piglets.
polyphenols from grape or hops are safe for the liver of piglet.

the effects of GME and SH on intestinal health and feed conversion in pigs are not due to changes of hepatic pathways linked with inflammation, the antioxidant system and stress of the endo-plasmic reticula.
